overview: Layer semantic tokens -> headless behavior primitives -> styled components -> product patterns. Define one controlled/uncontrolled ownership rule and forward refs. Publish tree-shakable per-component exports, semver changes and migration examples with visual, interaction and accessibility coverage. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

components.purpose: Layer semantic tokens -> headless behavior primitives -> styled components -> product patterns. Define one controlled/uncontrolled ownership rule and forward refs. Publish tree-shakable per-component exports, semver changes and migration examples with visual, interaction and accessibility coverage. Performance plan: 20 consuming apps, ~40 primitives; avoid bundling the full library for one button; measure consumer output, not source size. Accessibility: Define keyboard/focus contracts per primitive, native semantics first, contrast and reduced-motion tokens, accessible-name requirements and automated plus manual assistive-technology checks. Failure recovery: Document stable token/API contracts, use prerelease consumer validation, migration tooling and version rollback. Accessibility requirements are part of the API. Trade-off: Headless primitives maximize flexibility but consumers must style correctly. A styled system accelerates consistency but needs deliberate escape hatches; avoid unrestricted internal DOM dependencies.
